raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview Adds an opt-in Triton kernel that fuses the MLP gate/up GEMM with SiLU-and-mul for BF16 dense prefill on SM89 (RTX 4090), wired into `Qwen2MoeMLP`, the dense MLP of Qwen3.5-4B. Defaults are unchanged. Related: [RFC #52776](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52776) proposes a general epilogue interface; this PR is one narrow, measured instance and does not implement that interface. An open-PR search on 2026-11-03 (`swiglu gemm`, `silu fusion`, `dense MLP`, `52776`) found no equivalent dense BF16 gate/up + SiLU fusion for SM89; [#60846](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60846) targets SM120 tiny-batch decode (shared-expert scalar gate and reduction), not the gate/up GEMM. ## Claims - **End to end:** Qwen3.5-4B on one RTX 4090, 16K-token prompt, `vllm serve` default `max_num_batched_tokens=2048`: TTFT **−3.0%** (mean per-pair change, 95% CI −3.3% to −2.8%; median 1,143.5 → 1,108.2 ms over 12 request pairs, all 12 faster). - **Per MLP call (isolated op):** gate/up GEMM + SiLU-and-mul takes **10–11% less time** for 768–4,096 rows (1,090.1 → 966.2 µs, −11.4%, at 1,584 rows). - **Opt-in and contained:** nothing changes unless `+gated_linear_silu` is set. When it is set, steps outside 768–4,096 rows run the same cuBLAS GEMM and `silu_and_mul` kernels as before (bit-exact in the fallback tests), and no weight copy is made. GSM8K: 1,019 → 1,022 of 1,319 correct, difference not significant. ## Validation **Why this kernel.** In a 16K-token prefill before this PR, GEMMs take 73% of GPU kernel time and the MLP gate/up GEMM alone takes 30.5%. Its 18,432-wide BF16 output is written to memory only to be read back by SiLU-and-mul. The fused kernel keeps that intermediate in registers and writes the 9,216-wide activation once: ```text Before: X → gate/up GEMM → [G, U] in memory (M × 18,432, BF16) → SiLU(G) · U → A (M × 9,216) → down GEMM After: X → one kernel: gate/up GEMM with SiLU(G) · U in its epilogue → A (M × 9,216) → down GEMM ``` At 1,584 rows the skipped intermediate is about 58 MB per layer per step, written once and read once on the old path. Figure 1 sums kernel durations from one torch-profiler trace of a 16,384-token request on the tested base, taken after 3 warm-up requests (profiled TTFT within 0.5% of the unprofiled median). No after-change profile was taken; use of the fused kernel is shown by the dispatch test and by per-step counts (every fused 16K request ran all ten 1,584-row steps through it). **Kernel level.** Steps of 768–4,096 rows use the fused kernel; smaller steps keep the native kernels.
Numbers behind figure 2 (CUDA graphs, 8 rounds × 20 replays, arm order alternating each round) | Rows | Path | Native | Fused | Change | Per-round range | |---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 768 | fused | 500.2 µs | 451.2 µs | −9.8% | −10.7% to −8.8% | | 1,056 | fused | 728.8 µs | 646.9 µs | −11.2% | −11.9% to −10.6% | | 1,584 | fused | 1,090.1 µs | 966.2 µs | −11.4% | −12.9% to −9.6% | | 2,048 | fused | 1,316.5 µs | 1,186.4 µs | −9.9% | −10.7% to −8.9% | | 4,096 | fused | 2,631.6 µs | 2,371.3 µs | −9.9% | −10.5% to −7.4% | | 16 | native fallback | 106.9 µs | 107.0 µs | 0.0% | 0.0% to +0.1% | | 528 | native fallback | 376.9 µs | 377.0 µs | 0.0% | −0.1% to +0.1% | Native and fused are median times; Change is their ratio. The op is benchmarked in isolation with Qwen3.5-4B shapes and random BF16 weights.
**End to end.** One `vllm serve` at `b2a9480` with `--dtype bfloat16 --language-model-only --max-model-len 16576 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85` and the opt-in flag; everything else default (`max_num_batched_tokens` 2,048, FULL_AND_PIECEWISE CUDA graphs up to 512 tokens, prefix caching on). One request at a time, one output token, zero prefix-cache hits on every request. For the paired A/B, a test-only worker extension switches each MLP's `gate_up_silu` between the fused op and `None` while the server is drained, so both arms share KV allocation and the CUDA graphs captured at startup.
Numbers behind figure 3 (pairs run back-to-back, order alternating) | Prompt | Pairs | Median TTFT, native → fused | Mean per-pair change [95% CI] | Pairs slower | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 16,384 tokens | 12 | 1,143.5 → 1,108.2 ms | −3.04% [−3.32%, −2.77%] | 0 | | 528 tokens | 100 | 65.0 → 65.5 ms | +0.49% [−0.81%, +1.93%] | 58 | | 128 tokens | 100 | 40.8 → 41.0 ms | +1.25% [−0.09%, +2.55%] | 65 | CI: percentile bootstrap of the mean per-pair change, 10,000 resamples. A single 528- or 128-token request stays below 768 rows per step and never uses the kernel (batched short prompts can; see GSM8K below). The 528-token step runs eagerly through the enabled-but-unused op. The 128-token step replays the CUDA graph captured at startup in both arms, so that row is a noise control.
The kernel-level gain is enough to explain the end-to-end gain. A 16K prompt runs 10 steps of 1,584 rows through 32 layers, so 320 fused calls × 123.9 µs ≈ 39.6 ms would be expected from the isolated benchmark; the measured paired mean saving is 34.7 ms (95% CI 31.6–38.0 ms), about 87% of that. **Model quality.** GSM8K from the vLLM CI assets, 1,319 questions, 5-shot, greedy, concurrency 64: | | Native | Fused | |---|---:|---:| | Correct | 1,019 (77.26%) | 1,022 (77.48%) | Paired difference +0.23 pp, 95% CI −0.76 to +1.21 pp. The fused kernel processed 542,217 rows (counted at one representative layer). Because decode rows can share a step with prefill chunks, that covers 35–56% of the 972,038 prompt tokens: 56% if every row was a prompt row, 35% after subtracting all 203,366 generated tokens. Scheduling alone moves results at this concurrency: a native re-run of 64 questions changed 6 outcomes, while native and fused differ on 45 of 1,319. The kernel accumulates in a different order than cuBLAS, so outputs are not bitwise identical and greedy tokens can diverge (an earlier 4K-prompt probe diverged at token 58). **GPU sync check.** A real-server run with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` (guard confirmed active) served 528- and 16,384-token requests on both paths without error; the fused 16K request ran all ten 1,584-row steps through the kernel. **Reproduce.** ```bash # Correctness, fallback, torch.compile and CUDA-graph tests. # Recorded: 23 passed on RTX 4090, run standalone against the b2a9480 wheel # with the patch overlaid (exact command in REPRODUCE.md of the evidence ZIP). .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_gated_linear_silu.py -q # Kernel-level numbers behind figure 2 .venv/bin/python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_gated_linear_silu.py \ --tokens 16 528 768 1056 1584 2048 4096 --json gated-projection.json # Server configuration used for figure 3 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B --dtype bfloat16 --language-model-only \ --max-model-len 16576 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \ --compilation-config '{"mode": 0, "custom_ops": ["all", "+gated_linear_silu"]}' ``` The paired end-to-end runner, per-pair timings, per-question GSM8K outcomes and model/runtime hashes are in the [evidence package](https://github.com/Totoro-qaq/vllm/blob/e78ce6adf5725a5870d5e7ba303183cf7fa2fd31/benchmark-evidence/sm89-gated-projection/sm89-gated-projection-evidence.zip?raw=true) ([README: contents and provenance](https://github.com/Totoro-qaq/vllm/blob/e78ce6adf5725a5870d5e7ba303183cf7fa2fd31/benchmark-evidence/sm89-gated-projection/README.md); exact commands are in REPRODUCE.md inside the ZIP; ZIP SHA256 `301300822fe318d9b88c7a19d4f666b39235bb7ee35f85e166f71b73933f3b75`). GPU results come from vLLM `b2a9480` (official wheel with the three runtime files overlaid), Torch 2.14.0+cu130 and Triton 3.8.0. This branch is based on newer `main`; its changed files are byte-identical to the tested ones and `qwen2_moe.py` is unchanged between the two bases, but the GPU runs were not repeated on the newer base. **CI coverage.** Upstream CI has not run on this PR yet; locally, pre-commit passed, including mypy and the check that new tests are wired into Buildkite. `tests/kernels/test_gated_linear_silu.py` is collected by the `tests/kernels` catch-all job `:nvidia: (B200) Miscellaneous Kernels`. The op-level tests call `torch.ops.vllm.gated_linear_silu` directly, so on B200 they run the Triton kernel (numerics, dispatch trace, opcheck and `torch.compile`, CUDA-graph weight update) and the exact native fallbacks. `create_gated_linear_silu` returns `None` off SM89, so on B200 the factory tests stop at the capability check. Selection inside `Qwen2MoeMLP`, its batch-invariance and weight-offload exclusions, and all performance numbers were validated only on the RTX 4090 above. vLLM CI has L4 (SM89) agents; I can add this file to an L4 step if reviewers want SM89 coverage in CI. ## Details
What changes, and how invasive it is | File | Change | |---|---| | `vllm/kernels/triton/gated_linear_silu.py` | New Triton kernel (102 lines) | | `vllm/model_executor/layers/fusion/gated_linear_silu.py` | New custom op and eligibility checks (108 lines) | | `vllm/model_executor/models/qwen2_moe.py` | +11/−2: build the op when eligible; `forward` uses it | | `tests/kernels/test_gated_linear_silu.py` | New tests | | `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_gated_linear_silu.py` | Kernel benchmark | | `docs/design/sm89_gated_projection.md` | How to enable it, and its scope | - **Off by default.** Without `+gated_linear_silu`, or when any eligibility check fails, `gate_up_silu` is `None` and `Qwen2MoeMLP.forward` runs the original code. - **Eligibility (checked once when the model is built):** SM89; BF16; unquantized, bias-free linears on the automatic linear backend; TP=1; hidden size 2560 and intermediate size 9216; `silu_and_mul` custom op enabled; no LoRA, batch invariance, expert gate or weight offload. At runtime, steps outside 768–4,096 rows and non-contiguous inputs fall back to the native GEMM and `silu_and_mul`. - **Untouched:** scheduler, model runner, KV cache, weight loading and configs. Reverting deletes the five new files and the hook in `qwen2_moe.py`; no config field, weight layout or saved state is added.
Design, trade-offs and limitations - The kernel reads the original `[gate; up]` weight rows in interleaved order, so there is no transformed copy and in-place weight updates are seen. It accumulates in FP32 and keeps the native BF16 cast points after the projection, the SiLU and the product. - One fixed configuration: 64-row × 64-output-column tiles (128 interleaved gate/up weight rows), K step 32, 4 warps, 3 stages. M is a runtime argument, so one binary serves every eligible token count. - The gain depends on the batch budget. With prefix caching on (the default), Qwen3.5's hybrid cache ends each non-final prefill chunk on its 528-token block. With the `vllm serve` default of 2,048, a 16K prompt therefore runs as 10 × 1,584 rows (fused) plus 528- and 16-row tails (native). With the offline `LLM` default of 8,192 on the same GPU, non-final chunks are 7,920 rows, above the 4,096-row limit, so the same 16K prompt never reaches the kernel. - The kernel is a plain `@triton.jit` function, not registered with vLLM's JIT warmup (`docs/contributing/jit_kernel_warmup.md`), so it compiles on its first eligible call. With `max_num_batched_tokens=2048` that call is the 2,048-row startup profile run. If no startup step has 768–4,096 rows, the first eligible step compiles it while serving, and vLLM's JIT monitor logs a warning (or raises with `--jit-monitor-mode error`). A `VllmJitKernel` wrapper can be added if reviewers prefer. - Compilation mode: vLLM auto-enables breakable CUDA graphs for Qwen3.5 on NVIDIA, which selects compilation mode 0, whose default custom-op set is `all`. The flag keeps `all` because the fusion also needs the `silu_and_mul` custom op. With `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0` the model is torch-compiled instead and `all` would also switch every other custom op to its CUDA kernel; that configuration was not measured. - Measured on one RTX 4090 only. Other SM89 parts (L4, L20, L40S) differ in SM count and memory bandwidth, which is why the path is opt-in. Not measured: decode throughput, speculative decoding, image/video inputs (runs were text-only) and torch.compile mode. The shape check is deliberately specific to Qwen3.5-4B's 2560/9216 MLP; other shapes would need their own tile choice and measurements.
AI assistance (Codex, Claude) was used. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above. ---
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

With prefix caching on (the default), Qwen3.5's hybrid cache ends each non-final prefill chunk on its 528-token block. With the `vllm serve` default of 2,048, a 16K prompt therefore runs as 10 × 1,584 rows (fused) plus 528- and 16-row tails (native). With the offline `LLM` default of 8,192 on the same GPU, non-final chunks are 7,920 rows, above the 4,096-row limit, so the same 16K prompt never reaches the kernel. - The kernel is a plain `@triton.jit` function, not registered with vLLM's JIT warmup (`docs/contributing/jit_kernel_warmup.md`), so it compiles on its first eligible call. With `max_num_batched_tokens=2048` that call is the 2,048-row startup profile run. If no startup step has 768–4,096 rows, the first eligible step compiles it while serving, and vLLM's JIT monitor logs a warning (or raises with `--jit-monitor-mode error`). A `VllmJitKernel` wrapper can be added if reviewers prefer. - Compilation mode: vLLM auto-enables breakable CUDA graphs for Qwen3.5 on NVIDIA, which selects compilation mode 0, whose default custom-op set is `all`. The flag keeps `all` because the fusion also needs the `silu_and_mul` custom op. With `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0` the model is torch-compiled instead and `all` would also switch every other custom op to its CUDA kernel; that configuration was not measured. - Measured on one RTX 4090 only. Other SM89 parts (L4, L20, L40S) differ in SM count and memory bandwidth, which is why the path is opt-in. Not measured: decode throughput, speculative decoding, image/video inputs (runs were text-only) and torch.compile mode. The shape check is deliberately specific to Qwen3.5-4B's 2560/9216 MLP; other shapes would need their own tile choice and measurements.
AI assistance (Codex, Claude) was used. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above. ---

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Compare the native gate/up + SiLU chain with the gated-projection operation."""
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import statistics
+import time
+from pathlib import Path
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--tokens", type=int, nargs="+", default=[16, 528, 768, 1056, 1584, 2048, 4096]
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("--rounds", type=int, default=8)
+    parser.add_argument("--replays", type=int, default=20)
+    parser.add_argument("--json", type=Path)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    if min(args.tokens) < 1 or args.rounds < 1 or args.replays < 1:
+        parser.error("Token counts, rounds and replays must be positive")
+
+    import torch
+    import torch.nn.functional as F
+
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.fusion import gated_linear_silu  # noqa: F401
+    from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+    if not current_platform.is_cuda() or not current_platform.has_device_capability(80):
+        raise RuntimeError("This benchmark requires NVIDIA BF16 tensor cores")
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    stream = torch.cuda.Stream()
+    result = {
+        "device": current_platform.get_device_name(),
+        "capability": current_platform.get_device_capability(),
+        "torch": torch.__version__,
+        "scope": "Gate/up projection and activation; not full-model latency",
+        "persistent_weight_copy_bytes": 0,
+        "cases": [],
+    }
+
+    def capture(fn):
+        stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+        with torch.cuda.stream(stream):
+            for _ in range(5):
+                fn()
+        stream.synchronize()
+        graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+        with torch.cuda.graph(graph, stream=stream):
+            output = fn()
+        graph.replay()
+        torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+        return graph, output
+
+    def measure(graph):
+        start, end = (
+            torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True),
+            torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True),
+        )
+        start.record()
+        for _ in range(args.replays):
+            graph.replay()
+        end.record()
+        end.synchronize()
+        return start.elapsed_time(end) * 1000 / args.replays
+
+    with torch.inference_mode():
+        weight = torch.randn(18432, 2560, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda") * 0.05
+        for rows in args.tokens:
+            x = torch.randn(rows, 2560, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda") * 0.05
+
+            def native(x=x):
+                projected = F.linear(x, weight)
+                out = torch.empty((x.shape[0], 9216), dtype=x.dtype, device=x.device)
+                torch.ops._C.silu_and_mul(out, projected)
+                return out
+
+            def candidate(x=x):
+                return torch.ops.vllm.gated_linear_silu(x, weight)
+
+            torch.testing.assert_close(candidate(), native(), rtol=0.02, atol=0.02)
+            functions = {"native": native, "gated_op": candidate}
+            graphs = {name: capture(fn) for name, fn in functions.items()}
+            measurements = {
+                name: {"graph_us": [], "eager_us": []} for name in functions
+            }
+            for repeat in range(args.rounds):
+                order = list(functions)
+                if repeat % 2:
+                    order.reverse()
+                for name in order:
+                    measurements[name]["graph_us"].append(measure(graphs[name][0]))
+                    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+                    start = time.perf_counter()
+                    for _ in range(args.replays):
+                        functions[name]()
+                    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+                    measurements[name]["eager_us"].append(
+                        (time.perf_counter() - start) * 1e6 / args.replays
+                    )
+            row = {
+                "tokens": rows,
+                "path": "fused_prefill" if 768 <= rows <= 4096 else "native_fallback",
+                "samples": measurements,
+            }
+            for name, values in measurements.items():
+                row[name] = {
+                    key + "_median": statistics.median(samples)
+                    for key, samples in values.items()
+                }
+            result["cases"].append(row)
+            print(
+                json.dumps(
+                    {key: value for key, value in row.items() if key != "samples"}
+                )
+            )
+            del graphs
+    if args.json:
+        args.json.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + "\n")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

@@ -0,0 +1,30 @@
+# SM89 BF16 gated projection
+
+The dense Qwen MLP has an opt-in gate/up projection and SiLU-and-multiply fusion
+on SM89. Measurements used RTX 4090; other SM89 devices need their own performance
+qualification. The measured path targets BF16, hidden size 2560, intermediate size 9216,
+and 768–4096 input tokens. Other input sizes use the existing linear and
+activation operations, including captured decode graphs.
+
+This path requires unquantized linears, tensor parallel size one, the automatic
+linear backend, and no LoRA, weight offloading, or batch-invariant mode. Expert-gated MLPs and
+alternate linear or activation implementations keep their existing path.
+
+The kernel reads the original gate/up rows in paired order. It creates no
+transformed weight copy and sees weight updates at the original storage address.
+The token count is a runtime argument, so changing it does not require a kernel
+binary for every prefill size.
+
+Projection, SiLU, and product retain their BF16 cast boundaries. GEMM accumulation
+can differ from the vendor implementation; this optimization does not promise
+bitwise-identical generated tokens. Model-level quality checks remain necessary.
+
+Enable the path explicitly through the existing custom-op control:
+
+```console
+vllm serve MODEL --compilation-config '{"custom_ops": ["all", "+gated_linear_silu"]}'
+```
+
+The base mode `all` alone leaves this integration disabled. This avoids changing
+defaults based on measurements from a single GPU/model configuration. Keep your
+other custom-op overrides when adding this opt-in.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Correctness and integration contracts for the BF16 gated projection."""
+
+import json
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+
+from vllm.config import CompilationConfig, VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.activation import SiluAndMul
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fusion.gated_linear_silu import (
+    GatedLinearSilu,
+    create_gated_linear_silu,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.linear import (
+    MergedColumnParallelLinear,
+    RowParallelLinear,
+)
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not current_platform.is_cuda() or not current_platform.has_device_capability(80),
+    reason="The kernel requires NVIDIA BF16 tensor cores",
+)
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def single_rank(tmp_path):
+    from vllm.distributed import (
+        destroy_distributed_environment,
+        destroy_model_parallel,
+        init_distributed_environment,
+        initialize_model_parallel,
+        model_parallel_is_initialized,
+    )
+
+    if model_parallel_is_initialized():
+        yield
+        return
+    with set_current_vllm_config(VllmConfig()):
+        try:
+            init_distributed_environment(
+                world_size=1,
+                rank=0,
+                local_rank=0,
+                distributed_init_method=f"file://{tmp_path / 'distributed-init'}",
+                backend="nccl",
+            )
+            initialize_model_parallel(tensor_model_parallel_size=1)
+            yield
+        finally:
+            destroy_model_parallel()
+            destroy_distributed_environment()
+
+
+def reference(x, weight):
+    projected = F.linear(x, weight)
+    out = torch.empty(
+        (*projected.shape[:-1], projected.shape[-1] // 2),
+        dtype=x.dtype,
+        device=x.device,
+    )
+    torch.ops._C.silu_and_mul(out, projected)
+    return out
+
+
+def operands(rows, hidden=2560, intermediate=9216, dtype=torch.bfloat16):
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    return (
+        torch.randn(rows, hidden, dtype=dtype, device="cuda") * 0.05,
+        torch.randn(2 * intermediate, hidden, dtype=dtype, device="cuda") * 0.05,
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("rows", [768, 769, 1056, 1584, 2048, 4096])
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_gated_projection_preserves_declared_rounding(rows):
+    x, weight = operands(rows)
+    actual = torch.ops.vllm.gated_linear_silu(x, weight)
+    expected = reference(x, weight)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=0.02, atol=0.02)
+    relative_rmse = (actual.float() - expected.float()).square().mean().sqrt()
+    relative_rmse /= expected.float().square().mean().sqrt()
+    assert relative_rmse <= 0.0035
+    projected = (x[:16].double() @ weight.double().T).to(torch.bfloat16)
+    gate, up = projected.chunk(2, dim=-1)
+    activated = (gate.double() / (1 + torch.exp(-gate.double()))).to(torch.bfloat16)
+    precise = (activated.double() * up.double()).to(torch.bfloat16)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual[:16], precise, rtol=0.02, atol=0.02)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "rows,hidden,intermediate,dtype",
+    [
+        (16, 2560, 9216, torch.bfloat16),
+        (64, 2560, 9216, torch.bfloat16),
+        (528, 2560, 9216, torch.bfloat16),
+        (767, 2560, 9216, torch.bfloat16),
+        (4097, 2560, 9216, torch.bfloat16),
+        (768, 128, 65, torch.bfloat16),
+        (768, 2560, 9216, torch.float16),
+    ],
+)
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_ineligible_inputs_preserve_native_output_exactly(
+    rows, hidden, intermediate, dtype
+):
+    x, weight = operands(rows, hidden, intermediate, dtype)
+    actual = torch.ops.vllm.gated_linear_silu(x, weight)
+    expected = reference(x, weight)
+    assert torch.equal(actual.view(torch.uint8), expected.view(torch.uint8))
+
+
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_strided_input_uses_native_fallback():
+    x, weight = operands(768)
+    storage = torch.empty((768, 5120), dtype=x.dtype, device=x.device)
+    strided = storage[:, ::2]
+    strided.copy_(x)
+    actual = torch.ops.vllm.gated_linear_silu(strided, weight)
+    expected = reference(strided, weight)
+    assert torch.equal(actual.view(torch.uint8), expected.view(torch.uint8))
+
+
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_supported_prefill_executes_the_new_kernel_and_small_rows_do_not(tmp_path):
+    for rows, should_fuse in [(768, True), (528, False)]:
+        x, weight = operands(rows)
+        torch.ops.vllm.gated_linear_silu(x, weight)
+        torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+        with torch.profiler.profile(
+            activities=[
+                torch.profiler.ProfilerActivity.CPU,
+                torch.profiler.ProfilerActivity.CUDA,
+            ]
+        ) as profile:
+            torch.ops.vllm.gated_linear_silu(x, weight)
+            torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+        path = tmp_path / f"dispatch-{rows}.json"
+        profile.export_chrome_trace(str(path))
+        kernels = [
+            e["name"]
+            for e in json.loads(path.read_text())["traceEvents"]
+            if e.get("cat") == "kernel"
+        ]
+        assert kernels
+        assert (
+            any("_gated_linear_silu_kernel" in name for name in kernels) == should_fuse
+        )
+
+
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_schema_fake_and_compiled_runtime_shape_dispatch():
+    x, weight = operands(768)
+    torch.library.opcheck(
+        torch.ops.vllm.gated_linear_silu.default,
+        (x, weight),
+        test_utils=("test_schema", "test_autograd_registration", "test_faketensor"),
+    )
+    compiled = torch.compile(
+        torch.ops.vllm.gated_linear_silu, fullgraph=True, dynamic=True
+    )
+    for rows in [16, 768, 1584, 528]:
+        x, _ = operands(rows)
+        actual = compiled(x, weight)
+        expected = torch.ops.vllm.gated_linear_silu(x, weight)
+        assert torch.equal(actual.view(torch.uint8), expected.view(torch.uint8))
+
+
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_graph_replay_reads_updated_original_weight_storage():
+    x, weight = operands(768)
+    pointer = weight.data_ptr()
+    stream = torch.cuda.Stream()
+    stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+    with torch.cuda.stream(stream):
+        for _ in range(3):
+            torch.ops.vllm.gated_linear_silu(x, weight)
+    stream.synchronize()
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph, stream=stream):
+        output = torch.ops.vllm.gated_linear_silu(x, weight)
+    weight.zero_()
+    output.fill_(float("nan"))
+    graph.replay()
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    assert weight.data_ptr() == pointer
+    assert torch.equal(output, torch.zeros_like(output))
+
+
+def real_linears():
+    gate = MergedColumnParallelLinear(
+        2560,
+        [9216, 9216],
+        bias=False,
+        params_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+        disable_tp=True,
+    )
+    down = RowParallelLinear(
+        9216,
+        2560,
+        bias=False,
+        params_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+        disable_tp=True,
+    )
+    return gate, down, SiluAndMul(compile_native=False)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("mode", ["default", "enabled", "disabled"])
+def test_real_linear_factory_respects_custom_op_control(mode, single_rank):
+    custom_ops = {
+        "default": ["all"],
+        "enabled": ["all", "+gated_linear_silu"],
+        "disabled": ["all", "-gated_linear_silu"],
+    }[mode]
+    config = VllmConfig(compilation_config=CompilationConfig(custom_ops=custom_ops))
+    with set_current_vllm_config(config), torch.device("cuda"):
+        fused = create_gated_linear_silu(*real_linears())
+        if mode == "enabled" and current_platform.get_device_capability() == (8, 9):
+            assert isinstance(fused, GatedLinearSilu)
+        else:
+            assert fused is None
+
+
+def test_real_linear_factory_keeps_batch_invariant_path(monkeypatch, single_rank):
+    monkeypatch.setenv("VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT", "1")
+    config = VllmConfig(
+        compilation_config=CompilationConfig(custom_ops=["all", "+gated_linear_silu"])
+    )
+    with set_current_vllm_config(config), torch.device("cuda"):
+        assert create_gated_linear_silu(*real_linears()) is None
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("backend", ["uva", "prefetch"])
+def test_weight_offloading_keeps_native_linears(backend, single_rank):
+    from vllm.config.offload import (
+        OffloadConfig,
+        PrefetchOffloadConfig,
+        UVAOffloadConfig,
+    )
+
+    offload = (
+        OffloadConfig(uva=UVAOffloadConfig(cpu_offload_gb=1))
+        if backend == "uva"
+        else OffloadConfig(prefetch=PrefetchOffloadConfig(offload_group_size=2))
+    )
+    config = VllmConfig(
+        compilation_config=CompilationConfig(custom_ops=["all", "+gated_linear_silu"]),
+        offload_config=offload,
+    )
+    with set_current_vllm_config(config), torch.device("cuda"):
+        assert create_gated_linear_silu(*real_linears()) is None

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""BF16 gate/up GEMM with native-rounded SiLU-multiply epilogue."""
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.triton_utils import tl, tldevice, triton
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def native_round_silu_mul(gate, up):
+    # Match the native boundary: linear -> BF16, SiLU -> BF16, product -> BF16.
+    gate = gate.to(tl.bfloat16).to(tl.float32)
+    up = up.to(tl.bfloat16).to(tl.float32)
+    activated = tl.div_rn(gate, 1.0 + tldevice.exp(-gate))
+    activated = activated.to(tl.bfloat16).to(tl.float32)
+    return (activated * up).to(tl.bfloat16)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def tile_ids(M, N, BM: tl.constexpr, BN: tl.constexpr):
+    pid = tl.program_id(0)
+    pm, pn = tl.cdiv(M, BM), tl.cdiv(N, BN)
+    group_size = 8 * pn
+    group = pid // group_size
+    first = group * 8
+    actual = tl.minimum(pm - first, 8)
+    return first + (pid % group_size) % actual, (pid % group_size) // actual
+
+
+@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["M"])
+def _gated_linear_silu_kernel(
+    X,
+    W,
+    Y,
+    M,
+    K: tl.constexpr,
+    DFF: tl.constexpr,
+    XS0: tl.constexpr,
+    XS1: tl.constexpr,
+    WS0: tl.constexpr,
+    WS1: tl.constexpr,
+    BM: tl.constexpr,
+    BN: tl.constexpr,
+    BK: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    pm, pn = tile_ids(M, DFF, BM, BN)
+    rm = pm * BM + tl.arange(0, BM)
+    pair = 2 * pn * BN + tl.arange(0, 2 * BN)
+    raw_row = pair // 2 + (pair % 2) * DFF
+    rk = tl.arange(0, BK)
+    acc = tl.zeros((BM, 2 * BN), tl.float32)
+    for block in range(tl.cdiv(K, BK)):
+        kk = block * BK + rk
+        a = tl.load(
+            X + rm[:, None] * XS0 + kk[None, :] * XS1,
+            mask=(rm[:, None] < M) & (kk[None, :] < K),
+            other=0,
+        )
+        b = tl.load(
+            W + raw_row[None, :] * WS0 + kk[:, None] * WS1,
+            mask=(pair[None, :] < 2 * DFF) & (kk[:, None] < K),
+            other=0,
+        )
+        acc = tl.dot(a, b, acc)
+    gate, up = tl.split(tl.reshape(acc, (BM, BN, 2)))
+    rn = pn * BN + tl.arange(0, BN)
+    tl.store(
+        Y + rm[:, None] * DFF + rn[None, :],
+        native_round_silu_mul(gate, up),
+        mask=(rm[:, None] < M) & (rn[None, :] < DFF),
+    )
+
+
+def gated_linear_silu(x: torch.Tensor, weight: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Map BF16 ``x[M,K]`` and raw ``weight[2I,K]`` to a fresh BF16 ``out[M,I]``.
+
+    The caller validates dtype and supported shapes. Gate/up rows are read in
+    paired order without transforming or retaining a copy of the weight.
+    """
+    m, k = x.shape
+    d = weight.shape[0] // 2
+    out = torch.empty((m, d), dtype=x.dtype, device=x.device)
+    _gated_linear_silu_kernel[(triton.cdiv(m, 64) * triton.cdiv(d, 64),)](
+        x,
+        weight,
+        out,
+        M=m,
+        K=k,
+        DFF=d,
+        XS0=x.stride(0),
+        XS1=x.stride(1),
+        WS0=weight.stride(0),
+        WS1=weight.stride(1),
+        BM=64,
+        BN=64,
+        BK=32,
+        num_warps=4,
+        num_stages=3,
+        enable_fp_fusion=False,
+    )
+    return out

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Measured gate/up GEMM epilogue for unquantized SM89 dense prefills."""
+
+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+
+from vllm import envs
+from vllm.config import get_current_vllm_config_or_none
+from vllm.model_executor.custom_op import CustomOp
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.activation import SiluAndMul
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.linear import (
+    MergedColumnParallelLinear,
+    RowParallelLinear,
+    UnquantizedLinearMethod,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.utils import cuda_unquantized_gemm
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.utils.torch_utils import direct_register_custom_op
+
+
+def _gated_linear_silu(x: torch.Tensor, weight: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    if (
